e_100_eligible.quote: first query every eligible STEP 2 item ... carryover first (the newest SLOW record's "carryover:" line), then oldest due first, and write "eligible <n>: <keys>" to the run record; then work them in that order up to the per-run cap on Cadences
e_100_eligible.replay: Literal model: keys all 100, writes 'eligible 100: <100 keys>' (about 8 KB in one line, D7), works carryover then oldest due, each item one line sent/held/blocked/deferred. Holds and deferrals don't count toward the cap, so it keeps going until 40 sends in the run (FAST's sends included: LIMITS 'this run's own sends ... shared with your SLOW work'), 40 measured minutes or a tool error. Realistically about 15 to 30 items fit after FAST work; the rest go on 'carryover: <keys>' and are first next run. Risks: LIMITS still says stop when 'a hold applies' (D1); group order vs global oldest (D2); daily cap is not a named stop reason (D3); 'due today' may drop overdue items (D4).

f_stop_after_3_sends_at_7_min.quote: Stop only on that cap, the 40 minutes, or a tool error, naming which; stopping sooner with items left is a defect, Partial "stopped early: <why>".

Nothing forces a self-check before the last write (D6), and RUN RECORD in FAST still says 'Failed: stopped early' (D8).
